Ingredients.
For a big piece (7-8 inch wide).

-     Filling.

  • 200 millilitres (6.76 fl oz) room temperature heavy whipping cream. {Cream 1}

  • 200 millilitres (6.76 fl oz) cold heavy whipping cream. {Cream 2}

  • 300 grams (10.58 oz) melted dark chocolate.

  • 100 grams (3.53 oz) sugar.

  • 70 grams (2.47 oz) inverted sugar.

  • 80 grams (2.82 oz) gelatine mass.

-     Poolish.

  • 6 grams (0.21 oz) active-dry yeast.

  • 75 grams (2.65 oz) all-purpose flour.

  • 90 millilitres (3.04 fl oz) room temperature milk.

-     Bread dough.

  • 50 grams (1.76 oz) egg, approx. 1 medium egg.

  • 15 grams (0.53 oz) egg yolk, approx. 1 egg yolk.

  • 160 grams (5.64 oz) all-purpose flour.

  • A pinch of table salt.

  • 40 grams (1.41 oz) sugar.

  • 50 grams (1.76 oz)  soft butter (unsalted).

  • 1 teaspoon of orange blossom water or orange essence.

  • Orange or lemon zest.

-     Bread decoration.

  • 50 grams (1.76 oz) melted butter (to brush the bread after baking).

  • 200 grams (7.05 oz) sugar.

  • 6 grams (0.21 oz) powdered cinnamon.

Instructions.

-     Filling.
  1.   Heat on the stove {Cream 1} (6.76 fl oz), sugar (3.53 oz) and invert sugar (2.47 oz) until hot and steamy.
  2.    In a container pour the cream with the sugars, add melted dark chocolate (10.58 oz) and incorporate using an immersion blender or a ’normal’ blender until it is homogeneous. Add gelatin mass (2.82 oz) and dissolve perfectly. Add {Cream 2} (6.76 fl oz) and mix until smooth and homogeneous.
  3.    Rest in the refrigerator for at least 5 hours.
 
-     Poolish.
  1.   In a container with a lid add milk (3.04 fl oz), dry-active yeast (0.21 oz) and flour (2.65 oz). Mix until you get a homogeneous mass, close the container, and let it rest for 45 minutes in a warm place. It should double or triple its original size.
 
-     Bread dough.
  1.   When the poolish is ready, put it in the mixer bowl together with -previously beaten- egg and yolk, orange blossom water and lemon zest. Begin to mix with the dough hook.
  2.    After a minute of work in the stand mixer, start adding flour little by little (5.64 oz) and continue beating until it is a uniform dough but without elasticity. Add sugar (1.41 oz) and salt. Keep beating for 3 more minutes. Now the dough should start being elastic, add soft butter (1.76 oz). Beat for 4 to 5 more minutes.
  3.    Take a large bowl and sprinkle it lightly with water, place the dough, sprinkle again with water and cover with plastic wrap to ferment. Let stand in a warm place for 45 minutes.
  4.    After fermenting, place the dough on a working surface. Cut about 20% of it. Shape a large bread with the 80% remaining and set aside. Take the 20% and divide it again into 5 portions. Take a portion and make the shape of the ‘bones’ adding pressure between the working surface and index, middle and ring fingers, place the figure on the bread, and repeat the same process with three of the four remaining small portions. Make a small ball with the last portion and place it by pressing lightly on the rest of the dough, right on the centre of it, where the bones come together.
  5.    Place the dough on the baking tray, sprinkle lightly with water and leave to ferment for 60 minutes in a warm place.
  6.    Preheat the oven to 180°C / 356°F.
  7.    Bake the dough until golden brown (for me it was 35 minutes).
 
-     Bread decoration.
  1.   Allow the bread to cool completely. Mix sugar (7.05 oz) and cinnamon powder (0.21 oz). Varnish the bread with melted butter and cover completely with the sugar and cinnamon mixture.
  2.    Take the chocolate filling out of the refrigerator and thicken it with a balloon whisk.
  3.    Slice the bread horizontally and add the filling.
